identity.name: Najdat Kharijite emirate
alt_names: Najda's state in Najd and the Yamama

predecessors.note: The Najdat page: Najda 'launched a revolt against the Umayyad Caliphate' in 682.

land.text: Najd, Bahrain, Oman, Yemen and Ta'if

successors.note: 'Defeated by the caliphate in 693, at the battle of Mushahhar' (Najdat page).

rulers.name: Najda
rulers.title: leader (declared himself caliph c.687 per the Second Fitna page)
rulers.note: The Najdat page calls him 'leader'; murdered in 691.

rulers.name: Abu Fudayk
rulers.title: leader
rulers.note: 'Murdered Najda himself in 691 and took his place'; defeated in 693.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Najdat row; it gives the Umayyads Arabia in 682-691). The Najdat 'established an independent state in Najd and Yamama in 685' and 'held Bahrain, Oman, parts of Yemen' (Second Fitna page); the dates of Bahrain and Oman are not given.
New keyframe. Najda 'captured Yemen and Hadhramawt in 688' (Second Fitna page); the Najdat page has 687.

correction.text: 689-693: Najd, Bahrain, Oman, Yemen and Ta'if

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Najda 'occupied Ta'if in 689' (Second Fitna page); held, by my reading, until the defeat in 693 because no page gives another end.

region.text: Najd and the Yamama, the Najdat homeland

ledger.note: 685: Second Fitna page: Najda 'established an independent state in Najd and Yamama in 685'. The Najdat page: Najda 'launched a revolt against the Umayyad Caliphate' in 682 in the Yamama and Bahrain, and 'in 685, after some particular successes, the Kharijite faction of Abu Talut recognized Najda as their leader'. 685 is the state; 682 is the revolt.

Page silent on when. Second Fitna page: the Najdat 'held Bahrain, Oman, parts of Yemen' (undated). The Najdat page has the 682 revolt in 'the Yamama and Bahrain' but no conquest of Qatif or Oman. Placed with the state's founding (685).

region.text: Yemen and Hadhramawt, from the Zubayrids

ledger.note: Second Fitna page: Najda 'captured Yemen and Hadhramawt in 688'. The Najdat page dates it 687: 'In the same year [687], Najda invaded Yemen and seized it, including Sanaa', and his lieutenant Abu Fudayk 'conquered Hadramaut' that year; the Abd Allah page c.687/688. The Second Fitna year is used.

Second Fitna page: Najda 'occupied Ta'if in 689'. The Najdat page does not mention Ta'if; it says the Najdat began conquering the Hejaz after Ibn al-Zubayr's defeat, blocked supplies to Mecca and Medina and did not attack the holy villages.

region.text: Najd and Bahrain, attacked from Basra

ledger.note: 692: Najdat page: Abu Fudayk 'repelled a caliphate attack from Basra' in 692. The page does not say where the attack landed; the zone is the home lands (Najd and Bahrain), my reading.

region.text: Najd, Bahrain, Oman, Yemen and Ta'if, which the Najdat held

ledger.note: 693: Najdat page: 'they were eventually defeated by the caliphate in 693, at the battle of Mushahhar'. The page does not locate the battle or say which lands fell; the lands are those the Second Fitna page says they held, my reading.
693: the war ends with the defeat at Mushahhar (Najdat page). The page says the Najdat survived as a sect 'until around the tenth century'.

region.text: Najd and the Yamama, the Najdat homeland

ledger.note: 693: the Najdat state ends with the defeat at Mushahhar (Najdat page); Cliopatria's Umayyad shape of 692 already contains these lands.

wars.name: Najdat revolt
wars.outcome: Umayyad victory: the Najdat were 'eventually defeated by the caliphate in 693, at the battle of Mushahhar' (Najdat page).
wars.note: The revolt itself began in 682 in the Yamama and Bahrain; the state is dated from 685.

certainty.note: Tribal rule over the interior of Arabia; the pages list lands held, not borders, and date Bahrain and Oman nowhere.

sources.title: Najdat
sources.note: 682 revolt, 685 leadership, 687 Yemen, 691 murder of Najda, 692 attack from Basra, 693 Mushahhar.

sources.title: Second Fitna
sources.note: State in Najd and Yamama in 685, Yemen and Hadhramawt 688, Ta'if 689, Bahrain and Oman held.

notes: Written for group me-07 on 2026-10-19 from two pages. State Cliopatria lacks. Not on the pages: a capital (none named; the Yamama is the home region), where Mushahhar lay, what became of the Najdat holdings after Najda's death in 691, whether Ta'if was held to 693, when Bahrain and Oman fell, and the lands of the Najdat faction that split to Sistan in 687 (Atiyya ibn al-Aswad). The page disagreement over Yemen (687 on the Najdat page, 688 on the Second Fitna page) is kept in the event notes. Not to be confused with the dossier 'kharijites' (the Kharijite imamate of Ifriqiya, 751-761).
